title: Can AI Reviewers See Your Efforts to Improve Your Paper? A Large-Scale Study of Paper Revision Trajectories
summary: A study of 6,959 paper trajectories across five AI conferences found that eight AI reviewers often left scores unchanged after annotated major revisions, with weak agreement on score-change direction. Human confirmation covered a selected subset, so the result does not establish how reviewers generally respond across disciplines.
ai_technology: Eight AI reviewers independently scored versions from PaperTrajectory-2026
organization: MBZUAI; Virginia Tech; University of Maryland; University of Notre Dame

evidence.tested: The study analyzed 6,959 paper trajectories from five 2026 AI conferences. All eight reviewer models left scores unchanged on most revisions annotated as major improvements; a selected human subset checked annotations.
evidence.unknown: The dataset comprises papers from five AI conferences and human confirmation covers selected cases; findings do not establish behavior across all reviewers or scientific fields.
evidence.ai_role: Eight language-model reviewers independently scored versions from a dataset of paper revisions; a separate model annotated changes and overall quality, with human checks on a selected subset.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
